summary: ITERATION 2 — V17 retest after main agent fixes. Both action items from iter1 verified working: (1) newGame seeds 1 inbound IP offer at game start (sim.ts L299 returns generateInboundIPOffer(seeded)) and the offer 'Throne of Embers'/'Mighty Mechs' appears in /external-ip Inbound (1) immediately on Jan W1; (2) testID 'launch-service-btn' is present on streaming.tsx L78 and routes correctly to /streaming/launch. End-to-end flows exercised in browser: COUNTER modal opens with all c-fee/c-bo/c-merch/c-years/c-packs/c-excl/c-sub + submit-counter testIDs and submission updates state. ACCEPT path moves the offer from Inbound (1→0) into My Licenses (0→1) with correct fields (BO%, Merch%, Term, Packs). Outbound page loads gracefully (shows 'You don't own any franchises yet' instead of crashing). Streaming launch flow works: launch-service-btn → svc-name-input → confirm-launch creates the service. Streaming detail (/streaming/[id]) shows default Basic/Standard/Premium tiers and the player-service navigation works (via JS click — see minor issue below). Tier-picker testIDs (toggle-add-catalog, add-quick-all, add-quick-top, add-tier-{id}, confirm-add-tiers, cancel-add-tiers, edit-tier-access-{movieId}, edit-tier-{id}, save-tier-access) verified by source inspection in app/streaming/[id].tsx — gated on having released own movies which requires multi-week sim, skipped per request. Rivals catalog-pack exclusivity wiring (pick-exclusive-toggle → proposeBulkCatalogLicense({exclusivity}) → BulkCatalogOffer.exclusivity) verified in source.

ui_bugs.issue: testID 'player-service-{svcId}' is rendered TWICE on the streaming page (once in the 'Your Services' hero panel and once in the Industry Leaderboard list). Caused Playwright strict-mode violation; both elements share identical testID. Functionally the click works (one is hidden via overflow), but for testing automation the testID should be unique or scoped (e.g. 'hero-service-{id}' vs 'leaderboard-service-{id}').

action_items: OPTIONAL: Disambiguate duplicate testID 'player-service-{svcId}' on app/streaming.tsx (L39 hero card vs L96 leaderboard row). Use distinct testIDs so test automation can target each unambiguously.

OPTIONAL: Main agent self-test the full streaming tier-picker flow by creating a movie via /create-movie and ticking ~6 weeks until released, then exercising toggle-add-catalog → add-quick-all/add-quick-top → add-tier-{tierId} → confirm-add-tiers → edit-tier-access-{movieId} → save-tier-access. All testIDs verified present in code.

OPTIONAL: Self-test rivals catalog-pack exclusivity by navigating /rivals → relations → propose bulk catalog with pick-exclusive-toggle ON, then verify offer object has exclusivity:true (sim.ts proposeBulkCatalogLicense correctly forwards the flag and the news log includes 'EXCLUSIVE'). Wiring is correct per source review.

context_for_next_testing_agent: All V17 features wired correctly. To reach the streaming tier-picker UI in automation: launch a service (svc-name-input → confirm-launch), then on /streaming/[id] you need at least 1 released player-owned movie before toggle-add-catalog appears. To get a released movie: /create-movie → fill required fields → schedule release → simulate ~5-6 weeks via sim-week-btn. The 'License External Titles' picker (toggle-license-picker) is always visible and uses a different code path. For rivals exclusivity: /rivals → tap a rival with positive relations → propose bulk catalog license → toggle pick-exclusive-toggle → pick-propose-btn. The duplicated player-service-{id} testID across hero+leaderboard is a known minor issue — use .first or scoped queries in tests.
rca_of_issue: Both iter1 RCAs resolved. The seeding of 1 starter inbound IP offer at game start (sim.ts newGame) makes the COUNTER/ACCEPT/REJECT UI immediately reachable for testing & onboarding. The launch-service-btn testID makes the streaming launch CTA tappable in automation.
